scope_note: Core pager scope only, per Phase 0.5 brief. Denominator for the future completeness gate.

features.name: Startup: display file given as argument
features.behavior_summary: less opens and displays the contents of a named file, reading incrementally so large files start up fast.
fixture_needs: large file (startup speed not exact-value critical, but confirm no full-read block)
features.capture_notes: Baseline case; confirm first screen matches file head exactly (no extra banner).

features.name: Startup: display piped stdin
features.behavior_summary: less reads and displays input from a pipe when no filename is given; several options (-o/-O, %f prompt code) special-case pipe input vs a regular file.
fixture_needs: piped input larger than one screen
features.capture_notes: Man page does not enumerate this as a distinct top-level feature; existence inferred from -o/-O and %f wording. Confirm prompt differences (no filename) via capture.

features.name: Startup: multiple file arguments
features.behavior_summary: Multiple filenames on the command line are loaded into an ordered list; the first is displayed and the rest are reachable via :n/:p/:x.
fixture_needs: 3+ files to test :n/:p wraparound-vs-error at list ends

features.name: Scroll forward one line (default N=1)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls forward N lines, default 1. The entire N lines are displayed even if N exceeds the screen size.
features.capture_notes: man vs --help key-list differs slightly (--help omits ^J); trust man page COMMANDS as canonical enumeration.

features.name: Scroll backward one line (default N=1)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls backward N lines, default 1.

features.name: Scroll forward one window (default N=one window)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls forward N lines, default one window (screen height). If N exceeds the screen size, only the final screenful is displayed.

exact_values.default_N: window height (screen height, or as set by -z/z)

fixture_needs: Nf where N < window and N > window

features.name: Scroll backward one window (default N=one window)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls backward N lines, default one window. If N exceeds the screen size, only the final screenful is displayed.

features.name: Scroll forward one half-window (default N=half window)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls forward N lines, default one half of the screen size. If N is specified, it becomes the new default for subsequent d and u commands.
fixture_needs: d on odd-height window to determine rounding
Nd then bare d/u to confirm 'sticky' default
features.capture_notes: Exact half-window rounding (floor vs ceil vs round) for odd window heights is not stated in the man page; capture-determined.

features.name: Scroll backward one half-window (default N=half window)
features.behavior_summary: Scrolls backward N lines, default one half of the screen size. If N is specified, it becomes the new default for subsequent d and u commands.
features.capture_notes: Same rounding ambiguity as nav-forward-halfwindow; d and u share one 'half-window' default value per man page.

features.name: Go to line N (default: first line)
features.behavior_summary: Goes to line N in the file, default 1 (beginning of file). May be slow if N is large.

features.name: Go to line N (default: last line)
features.behavior_summary: Goes to line N in the file, default the end of the file.

features.name: Numeric prefix N for scroll/jump commands
keys_or_flags: N<cmd> for j k e y d u f b g G etc.
features.behavior_summary: Commands marked with * accept a preceding decimal number N which parameterizes that specific command per its own documented rule.
features.capture_notes: General mechanism; per-command exact effect captured under each nav-* feature.

features.name: UpArrow/DownArrow/PageUp/PageDown key bindings
features.behavior_summary: Expected to alias to k/j (line) and b/f (window) respectively via terminfo, but this mapping is not explicitly documented in man less or --help.
fixture_needs: send raw terminfo escape sequences for each key and observe resulting scroll amount
features.capture_notes: Not documented in man page or --help at all; fully capture-determined.

features.name: Forward search
features.behavior_summary: Searches forward for the N-th line (default 1) matching a regular-expression pattern; case-sensitive by default; starts at the first displayed line (subject to -a/-j).

features.name: Backward search
features.behavior_summary: Searches backward for the N-th line matching a pattern, starting at the last displayed line (subject to -a/-j).

features.name: Repeat last search (same direction)
features.behavior_summary: Repeats the previous search for the N-th next occurrence, same direction and modifiers as the original.

features.name: Repeat last search (reverse direction)
features.behavior_summary: Repeats the previous search but in the reverse direction.

features.name: Search match highlighting
features.behavior_summary: By default, ALL strings on screen matching the last search command are highlighted (not just the found occurrence).
fixture_needs: screen with multiple matches, verify all are highlighted
features.capture_notes: Exact terminal rendering (standout vs color) of highlight is capture-determined.

features.name: Search failure message
features.behavior_summary: less shows a status message when a search pattern is not found in the file.
features.capture_notes: Literal message text is fully capture-determined; man page never states it.

features.name: -N / --LINE-NUMBERS (line numbers)
features.behavior_summary: -N displays a line number at the start of every line; -n (default) suppresses them.
fixture_needs: line numbers vs long-line wrap interaction
features.capture_notes: Field width default of 7 is from --line-num-width doc; confirm actual left-padding format.

features.name: -S / --chop-long-lines
features.behavior_summary: Truncates lines longer than the screen width instead of wrapping; default (no -S) wraps long lines onto the next display line.
fixture_needs: line longer than terminal width, with and without -S

features.name: -R / --RAW-CONTROL-CHARS (ANSI passthrough)
features.behavior_summary: Passes ANSI color escape sequences (ESC[...m) and OSC 8 hyperlink sequences through raw; other control chars still use caret notation. Color resets to normal at the start of every line.
fixture_needs: ANSI color spanning multiple lines to confirm per-line reset
non-color ESC sequence with -R (should not be raw)

features.name: Default wrap / tab expansion / control-char caret notation
features.behavior_summary: Default: long lines wrap to next display line; tabs expand to 8-column stops; control characters shown in caret notation (e.g. ^A) or hex-in-angle-brackets fallback (LESSBINFMT default '*s<%02X>').
fixture_needs: line requiring wrap at exact terminal width boundary

features.name: :n / :p (next/previous file)
features.behavior_summary: :n examines the next file from the command-line list (or N-th next); :p examines the previous file (or N-th previous).
features.capture_notes: Exact message/behavior at list boundaries is capture-determined (man page doesn't state it).

features.name: '(file N of M)' prompt indicator
features.behavior_summary: Prompt escape '?m(%T %i of %m).' shows '(file N of M)' whenever more than one input file is open; %T is 'file' unless using -t tags mode.
fixture_needs: 2-file and 3-file sessions, capture literal prompt text at each position

features.name: Exit commands
features.behavior_summary: All exit less.

features.name: Exit status codes
features.behavior_summary: Only documented value is -K/--quit-on-intr producing exit code 2 on interrupt. Normal quit (q/Q/:q/:Q/ZZ) exit code is not documented.
features.capture_notes: Normal-quit and error-path exit codes are fully capture-determined.

features.name: Initial-screen filename display
features.behavior_summary: Prompt escape '?n?f%f.' shows the filename only on the first prompt shown for a newly opened file.
fixture_needs: first screen of a freshly opened file, capture exact prompt line text/position

features.name: Default short ':' prompt
features.behavior_summary: Default prompt format: '?n?f%f .?m(%T %i of %m) ..?e(END) ?x- Next\: %x..%t'.
features.capture_notes: Whether the prompt line uses reverse video/standout by default is not documented; capture-determined.

features.name: '(END)' marker at end-of-file
features.behavior_summary: Prompt escape '?e(END).' displays literal '(END)' when the display has reached end-of-file.
fixture_needs: scroll to EOF and capture prompt line

features.name: Byte offset / percent-into-file display rules
features.behavior_summary: Medium/long prompts include byte offset and/or percent-into-file, computed from the top/middle/bottom/target line depending on the escape's suffix character.
fixture_needs: -m and -M sessions across several scroll positions, capture literal byte/percent numbers vs actual file offsets

features.name: Error message display + bell behavior
features.behavior_summary: less rings the terminal bell by default on errors (e.g. scroll past EOF/BOF, invalid key); -q silences only the EOF/BOF-scroll bell, -Q silences all bells (visual bell substituted if available).
fixture_needs: trigger invalid-key error, capture message text
features.capture_notes: Exact error message strings are capture-determined; only the bell-ringing rule is documented.

features.name: Redraw on terminal resize
features.behavior_summary: Default window size (screen height, or screen-height-minus-offset via -z-N) auto-adjusts on resize; fractional -j/-# values are recalculated on resize; LESS_LINES/LESS_COLUMNS can override detected size and force full repaint on every movement.

exact_values.resize_example: 24-line screen with -z-4 => 20-line window; resized to 40 lines => 36-line window

fixture_needs: tmux pane resize mid-session, capture full repaint sequence
resize while mid-file (not at top) to see recentering behavior
features.capture_notes: Procedural redraw sequence/timing is not documented; capture-determined.

features.name: ESC sequence handling
features.behavior_summary: ESC is the escape-key prefix for two-character commands (e.g. ESC-v); under -R, only ANSI color (ESC[...m) and OSC 8 (ESC]8;...BEL/ESC\\) sequences are passed raw, governed by LESSANSIENDCHARS/LESSANSIMIDCHARS.
fixture_needs: non-standard ANSI mid/end chars via env override

features.name: UTF-8 character set handling
features.behavior_summary: UTF-8 mode is selected via LESSCHARSET/LESSCHARDEF, or auto-detected from LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG containing 'UTF-8'/'UTF8'/'utf-8'/'utf8', else via setlocale(), else defaults to utf-8. UTF-8 is the only charset supporting multi-byte characters.

exact_values.utf8_bin_fmt_default: <U+%04lX> (LESSUTFBINFMT; applies to problematic VALID Unicode codepoints only)
exact_values.malformed_utf8_byte_format: per-byte LESSBINFMT '<%02X>' e.g. '<E4><B8>' — capture-confirmed 2026-08-08; man page interpretation corrected by hub
